name: tpl-precedence-4-goal
task: Reach the exit, but you must have flipped the switch first.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task says the agent must flip the switch first, then reach the exit. The clauses express that: Existence(at_exit) is hard, and Precedence(switch_toggled, at_exit) is hard. But the reward machine has no Precedence-as-order check that the switch toggle must be a required goal. The clause Existence(at_exit) with Precedence(switch_toggled, at_exit) does not force switch_toggled to occur: the compiler clue says every way to finish includes switch_toggled, which is correct only because the machine's final state requires both. The clauses are consistent with the task, so no correction is needed in the clause set itself; however the reward structure in the machine is not part of what I critique. No changes are required to the clauses as written.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(at_exit) is the hard goal of reaching the exit, and Precedence(switch_toggled, at_exit) hard enforces that the switch is flipped first. The hard Existence(at_exit) with the hard Precedence chain already forces switch_toggled, so the compiled machine's finishing requirement matches the task.

texts: Reach the exit (the agent must end the episode standing on the exit cell)
The switch must be flipped before the agent reaches the exit; the toggle comes first, then the exit
machine:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
REJECTING_STATES: u2
DEFAULT_REWARD: 0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, !at_exit&switch_toggled) -> u1
(u0, at_exit&!switch_toggled) -> u2
(u0, at_exit&switch_toggled) -> u3
(u1, at_exit) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, !at_exit&switch_toggled, u1) -> 1
(u0, at_exit&!switch_toggled, u2) -> -10
(u0, at_exit&switch_toggled, u3) -> 12
(u1, at_exit, u3) -> 11
